text: Hello, everyone.Welcome back.Today, we are going to deal with the writing section.In this period, you will learn about the formal emails in terms of layout, content, and language.You are also expected to write a formal email to make inquiries about an English course in the UK, using the correct layout and proper language.Before class, please get your textbooks and worksheets ready.As globalization is approaching, the world is getting smaller.It's easier for us language learners to get exposed to the real language environment.Here comes an advertisement about a summer camp for English learners.Would you please read the advertisement and answer the following questions?You will have the next 30 seconds for that.Have you found the answers?The courses start on July 14th and August 10th.Also, they last for four weeks.They cost 900 pounds.Number four, students can also enjoy fun evening and weekend activities.Number five, we can contact more sham college for more details.And a good way is to make inquiries through emails.Here, we have two emails from Li Ming and Zhang Hui.Would you please read them and figure out their inquiries and reasons?You will have two minutes for that.Here, we have two emails from Li Ming.Would you please read them and figure out their questions?Now, let's check the answers.Li Ming was wondering whether he could stay with an English family.Because he wanted to practice his English.He would like to have some milk-free options, as he was not used to milk and ice cream.He also asked whether it would cost less money, because he could only do the course for three weeks.As for Zhang Hui, he wondered whether it could be cheaper if he stayed with his friend off campus.He wanted to improve his writing, so he inquired whether there would be a writing course.Also, he asked for more information about fun activities.Now, let's look at two emails.Does the layout look familiar to you?Does it remind you of the letter writing we learned in the first unit last term?But is there any difference between the two types of writing?If you look closely, you may find that both letters and emails include a salutation, a body, and a closing.However, an email should also include a subject heading, so that the recipient can have a clear idea of the email's content.Then, let's focus on the main part of the email.Would you please read the body part again and figure out what is included?You will have one minute for that.It's easy to find that the body part of both emails includes the writing purpose, the inquiries and reasons, and also the author's gratitude.And what about their writing styles?Are they similar to or different from each other?Would you please read the two emails again and figure it out?This time, you may focus on the language they've used, and you will have 90 seconds.You may focus on the language they've used, and you will have 90 seconds.How's it work?Their writing styles are quite different, right?One is quite formal, while the other is not.But what makes you think so?Let's hear your peers' ideas.Great!The opener and the closer can indicate whether an email is formal or not.Well, I found that Li Ming's sentences are shorter, such as, please write soon.However, Zhang Hui's sentences are longer.For example, I would be grateful if you could reply as soon as possible.Good!Shorter sentences and even imperatives 其始句 can be seen in informal emails.By contrast, requests are longer informal ones.And what else?Li Ming used the word advert, while Zhang Hui used advertisement.Also, Li Ming wrote your, but Zhang Hui didn't.He wrote the full form, like I did not.I think in Li Ming's email, the word cool is quite informal, which can rarely be seen in formal writing.That's right!Slangs such as cool can make one's writing less formal.Do you have evidence in their writing?This is what I have found.In Li Ming's writing, he wrote, please tell me more about.It would be cool too.And if I did, would it?In Zhang Hui's email, he wrote, please could you give me?I would be very grateful if you could.Both of them used the words please, could, would and etc.to show politeness.After comparing the two writing styles, which one do you think is more proper if you write to a college?In my opinion, informal pieces of writing include blogs, diaries, emails and letters to those you are quite familiar with.While formal pieces of writing include job applications, emails and letters to those you don't know well.Thus, the formal writing style seems more appropriate here.And before we move on, let's first review what we have learned.What should we pay attention to when we write a formal email to make inquiries?If you are to work out a checklist for it, what items will you include?You will have the next 30 seconds to think about it.Time's up!For me, I will ask myself 3 questions when I write a formal inquiry email.Does my email include a Subject heading, A Salutation, A Body and a Closing?第2點,我的電郵的身體部份含有寫字的目標,明確的詢問和原因,以及我的感謝給獎項者。第3點,是否語言正確的作為一個正式的電郵?現在,大家,是你們的機會。想像一下你們去摩山大學的夏天露營。你還想知道什麼?我的朋友住在 Brighton,所以我想知道他住在摩山多遠。我可以給我的朋友一個星期的旅遊嗎?請做兩份詢問,並提供原因。你會有一分鐘。你發自自己著想的是什麼?你想知道你老師的想法嗎?
